data.content_ref: inline:The target asserts a single mechanism — evapotranspiration deficit — but the problem demands the single mechanism that best explains why the nocturnal gap is larger in some cities than in others. If vegetation/irrigation were the dominant cross-city modulator, arid cities (minimal vegetation, almost no irrigation) should exhibit the largest nocturnal UHI. Empirically the opposite occurs: many arid cities have negligible or even negative nocturnal UHI, while dense humid-temperate cities with substantial vegetation show the strongest effect. The target's own countercondition concedes this, yet the claim is asserted as primary without resolution, so the mechanism fails as the single best explanation.
